Why I stopped at round 3

The two lowest dimensions are limited by missing evidence, not effort. No photo shows the north or east sides, the bathroom, or the upstairs landing, and the interior photos can't fix depth precisely. More rounds would only polish rendering, worth one or two points at most. New photos are what would move the score; the list is at the end.

Round 1 → 2

Mullion tops in #11 sat 0.07–0.17 m above the model's roof line. Refitting all six upper mullions gave z = 4.97 − 0.427·s, which #17 confirmed independently on the west wall. Ridge raised 4.80 → 4.95 m, eaves lowered to 2.17 m, roof depth 0.30 → 0.36 m to match the apex, and the header band clipped under the eave. The raise also resolved the bedroom-height conflict with #3 (2.4 → 2.55 m). Added surface textures, lighting modes and lamp-lit interiors. Furniture moved per the overhead photo #18.

Round 2 → 3

The glass read white and the soffits glowed. Causes: a studio environment map, and lamps lighting through walls because they cast no shadows. Fixes: a forest-gradient environment in world space, faster lamp falloff, darker glass, weathered deck tone. Geometry unchanged.

Checks that didn't work

A ray-cast of #12's furniture placed the first stair step outside the house, so that camera can't measure depth and was used for the west wall only. A floor homography from #18 failed because the wall bases are hidden behind furniture. I didn't substitute guessed points.

What would close the gap

  1. One photo of the northeast corner from outside, plus the north and east sides. This settles the ridge height and the unseen walls.
  2. The bathroom, and the upstairs landing looking back at the bedroom door.
  3. Total square footage from the listing, as a cross-check on the 6.5 m footprint.
